_note: Hand-maintained content for the History page (#history). The daily update never touches this file. Honours checked against Wikipedia's Liverpool F.C. records page in October 2026 (no major trophy in 2025-26). Add a new trophy by bumping its count and adding the year; add a legend under the right decade.

players.name: Alex Raisbeck
players.why: Captained Liverpool to their first two league titles, 1901 and 1906.

players.name: Elisha Scott
players.why: Kept goal for over 20 years, including the back-to-back titles of 1922 and 1923.

players.name: Gordon Hodgson
players.why: South African-born goal machine and one of the club's highest scorers.

players.name: Billy Liddell
players.why: Won the 1947 title and was so central to the 1950s side it was nicknamed “Liddellpool”.

players.name: Roger Hunt
players.why: The club's record league goalscorer and a 1966 World Cup winner.

players.name: Ian St John
players.why: Scored the extra-time winner in the 1965 FA Cup final.

players.name: Ron Yeats
players.why: Shankly's “colossus” and the first Liverpool captain to lift the FA Cup.

players.name: Ian Callaghan
players.why: Holds the club appearance record: 857 games.

players.name: Kevin Keegan
players.why: Spearheaded the 1973 and 1976 league and UEFA Cup doubles.

players.name: Ray Clemence
players.why: Won five league titles and three European Cups.

players.name: Emlyn Hughes
players.why: Captain who lifted the club's first European Cup, in Rome in 1977.

players.name: Kenny Dalglish
players.why: Scored the winner in the 1978 European Cup final; won the 1986 double as player-manager.

players.name: Ian Rush
players.why: The club's all-time top scorer, with 346 goals.

players.name: Graeme Souness
players.why: Captained the 1984 treble: league, League Cup and European Cup.

players.name: Alan Hansen
players.why: Elegant defender who won eight league titles.

players.name: Bruce Grobbelaar
players.why: His “spaghetti legs” helped win the 1984 European Cup shoot-out.

players.name: John Barnes
players.why: Lit up the 1988 and 1990 title sides; Footballer of the Year twice.

players.name: Robbie Fowler
players.why: Home-grown striker known to the Kop simply as “God”.

players.name: Steve McManaman
players.why: Home-grown winger who scored both goals in the 1995 League Cup final.

players.name: Steven Gerrard
players.why: Captain who led the comeback in Istanbul in 2005.

players.name: Jamie Carragher
players.why: One-club man, second only to Callaghan in appearances.

players.name: Michael Owen
players.why: Won the Ballon d'Or in 2001, the year of the cup treble.

players.name: Sami Hyypiä
players.why: Commanding defender of the 2001 treble and Istanbul 2005.

players.name: Xabi Alonso
players.why: Scored the equaliser in the 2005 Champions League final.

players.name: Fernando Torres
players.why: Scored 24 league goals in his first season.

players.name: Luis Suárez
players.why: Player of the Year in 2014 after 31 league goals.

players.name: Jordan Henderson
players.why: Captain who lifted the 2019 Champions League and the 2020 league title.

players.name: Mohamed Salah
players.why: Scored a then-record 32 goals in the 2017–18 Premier League season.

players.name: Sadio Mané
players.why: Relentless forward of the 2019 and 2020 triumphs.

players.name: Virgil van Dijk
players.why: Transformed the defence; captain of the 2024–25 title side.

players.name: Alisson Becker
players.why: Goalkeeper of the 2019 Champions League win, who also scored a headed winner in 2021.

players.name: Trent Alexander-Arnold
players.why: Home-grown full-back behind the quick corner that beat Barcelona in 2019.

moments: The first FA Cup: Leeds beaten 2–1 after extra time.
Rome: the first of six European Cups.
A treble: league, League Cup and European Cup.
League and FA Cup double, with Dalglish as player-manager.
A cup treble: League Cup, FA Cup and UEFA Cup.
Istanbul: 3–0 down at half-time, champions of Europe on penalties.
Madrid: a sixth European Cup, then the Club World Cup.
The first league title in 30 years.
